headline: power is at a three-year high and gas at a new high for this run, and this time the winter months led the rise
commentary: UK power spot is 180.49 £/MWh, its highest in more than three years, up 6.0% since our update on 22 October and 135% above where it was a year ago. Gas has moved with it. The November contract is 233.99 p/therm, up 4.5% since Thursday and about 12.6% above September's peak, another new high for this run. On Friday the system operator, NESO, forecast a 9.5% margin of spare capacity above peak demand this winter, slightly more than its earlier view. Analysts called that credible. That margin is about keeping the lights on. Prices still follow gas, and the gas risks reported last week stand: record-low European storage and the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Forecasters expect a mild, wet and windy end to the year, but seasonal models point to colder risk in February, and analysts warn a long cold spell with tight gas would push prices up. This time the front of the curve led: November to March are up 4.2 to 4.6%, Winter 27 2.8%. So the step down from this winter to next widened, from 26.8% to 28.0%, and a longer contract blends this winter with cheaper years. On the winter months alone, a 12-month contract from November is about 0.37 p/kWh higher on a wholesale-equivalent basis than on Thursday. Waiting has now cost money in all five updates since late September. Day-ahead prices this week ran from £150.47/MWh on 21 October down to £4.86 over the weekend. That swing is the exposure a fixed price removes.

gas.note: NBP front month Nov 26 is 233.99 p/therm, up 4.5% on its 22 Oct print of 223.85 and about 12.6% above September's peak, a new high for this run. The rest of this winter: Dec 26 236.30, Jan 27 237.46, Feb 27 235.49, Mar 27 223.07, Q1 27 233.50. This time the front of the curve rose faster than the back: the winter months are up 4.2 to 4.6%, against Winter 27 168.20 (+2.8%), Summer 28 106.00 (+4.4%) and Winter 28 110.00 (+2.7%). So the step down from this winter widened: Q1 27 to Winter 27 is a 28.0% discount, from 26.8% on 22 Oct. A rise across the whole curve means a longer contract does not dodge the increase, but it blends this winter down with cheaper years.
